deep.reconstruction: Notation: Euler's ∫(1/z^m)(1/y^n) is S(m,n) = Σ_{z≥1} z^{-m} Σ_{y≤z} y^{-n} = ζ(m,n) + ζ(m+n), where ζ(m,n) = Σ_{z>y} z^{-m} y^{-n} is the strict double zeta value. ∫1/z^k is ζ(k). This page finishes 'Ordo nonus' (weight m+n = 10), which has 9 series S(m,10−m). The 'first method' (§19, previous page) is the stuffle relation S(m,n)+S(n,m) = ζ(m)ζ(n)+ζ(m+n). The 'second method' is a partial-fraction / shuffle-type method. On this page it gives four things. (i) S(9,1) = 3ζ2ζ8 − ζ3ζ7 + 3ζ4ζ6 − ½ζ5² − (11/2)ζ10. (ii) Two equations that reduce only to the known identity ζ10 = (10/11)ζ4ζ6. (iii) S(6,4)+S(7,3) = 6ζ4ζ6 − ζ5² − (7/2)ζ10. (iv) 2S(7,3)+7S(8,2) = 14ζ3ζ7 − 45ζ4ζ6 + 8ζ5² + 33ζ10. One determination is therefore still missing for weight 10. In §20 Euler takes stock. Only orders 1, 2, 3, 5 (weights 3, 4, 5... i.e. m+n = 2, 3, 4, 6) are fully determined; every other order lacks exactly one relation. For even weight, the method reproduces the rational relations among ζ(2), ζ(4), ζ(6), ... (his earlier results) without any appeal to π or the quadrature of the circle. The next page adds his surprise: no analogous relations among odd zeta values ever appear. He then lists the general closed form for S(2k−1,1). Modern reading: double-shuffle relations at weight 10 leave exactly one free parameter, the irreducible ζ(7,3).
errors: No mathematical errors. All four relations were checked by solving the full stuffle plus shuffle system at weight 10. With x_j = ζ(j,10−j): x3+x4 = P+Q−2ζ10 and 7x2+2x3 = 28.05ζ10 − 12P − 8Q, where P = ζ3ζ7 and Q = ζ5². These give (iii) and (iv) exactly. (i) agrees with Euler's ζ(m,1) formula once one uses 4ζ2ζ8 + 4ζ4ζ6 = 11ζ10, and ζ10 = (10/11)ζ4ζ6 is also correct.

This is a limitation rather than an error: his 'one determination missing' is genuine at weights 8 and 10, where ζ(5,3) and ζ(7,3) are irreducible. At odd weights 5, 7, 9 all double zetas are in fact reducible, so there the missing determination reflects incompleteness of his second method, not a true obstruction.

deep.surprise_reason: E477 is the well-studied origin of double zeta values. Its weight-by-weight relations and Euler's remark on the missing determination (irreducibles at weights 8 and 10) are routinely cited, as is his observation about odd zeta values. All results check out, but none appear absent from the literature.
